answer.read: Blankstahl wants volume and planning security [Z volume strong, planning_security moderate]. It wants an AS-14404 clause because it will not fix prices for a long term [S latest e-mail; Z material_risk_protection]. It has already moved fast, from €6.14 to €5.40, and accepted our 36 months and 60 days [S]. Its status is open, not final. It is a family firm reviewing small accounts, so we should not squeeze it brutally [Z deprioritising_us]. Its full cost is estimated around €5.49 with about ±5% error [E], so the current price is already close to its cost.
answer.message: Thank you for moving quickly and for agreeing to the longer commitment and our payment terms. We understand your need for protection on the alloy surcharge and can accept an AS-14404 clause with a deadband, which shares the real material risk fairly between us. On that basis we propose the attached terms, which reflect the price level we have been paying for this part. We value a stable, long-term partnership with you.
answer.reason: o9 gives the supplier the index clause it insists on. The wide deadband keeps the clause cheap for us (about €2.2k over the horizon), and our cost C of roughly €242.3k is close to the lowest available. E0 has a similar C but uses a db 0 % clause that costs us much more. The no-clause options ignore its stated hard requirement and would likely stall. The 24-month term limits our exposure, although the supplier may want 36 months. Its pace suggests it will come back with a counter between its offer and ours, so accepting now would leave value on the table. Citing our order history at €5.84 anchors the price below its sheet.
